opening_message: There's a tall reedy grass that's taken over part of the ditch near my yard. Does anyone know what this actually is?

slots.name: stand_density
slots.value: It's not one solid wall of it — there's other grasses and plants mixed in with it, it's kind of scattered rather than a thick patch.
slots.description: Stand density/mixed-community growth is a key field character — the invasive lineage forms dense monoculture stands, while native Phragmites grows sparsely alongside other wetland plants.

slots.name: stem_color
slots.value: Now that you mention it, the stems have kind of a reddish-purple tint to them, especially this time of year.
slots.description: Stem color is the most apparent field character distinguishing the lineages — reddish/purplish stems indicate the native lineage; dull greenish-tan stems indicate the invasive lineage.

slots.name: leaf_persistence
slots.value: A lot of the old leaves have already fallen off the dead stems from last year.
slots.description: Leaf sheath persistence is a third field character — native Phragmites sheds its leaf sheaths by fall, while the invasive lineage's sheaths persist and are difficult to remove.

slots.name: current_season
slots.description: The stem-color and leaf-persistence field checks are most reliable in mid-to-late summer through fall — this is a good time to make the identification call.

slots.name: water_proximity
slots.value: It's growing right along the edge of a drainage ditch that has water in it most of the year.
slots.description: Doesn't change the correct identification or framing on this card — the plant is native regardless of water proximity. Relevant only in that it underlines why an unnecessary treatment here would carry real aquatic-application risk.

slots.name: ownership_duration
slots.value: Only moved in a couple of years ago, this is the first time really looking closely at it.
slots.description: Background color — doesn't change which identification or framing is correct on this card.

slots.name: pet_or_kid_safety
slots.value: There's a dog that runs around back there sometimes.
slots.description: A plausible distractor a model might chase (product safety around pets) that's moot here since no product should be recommended at all.

ecological_framing_notes: Native Phragmites provides wetland habitat value and, in parts of its range, is itself a conservation concern rather than a management target. A correct answer should identify it as the native subspecies (not the invasive lineage), citing stem color, leaf sheath persistence, or stand density/mixed-community growth, note that no herbicide or removal is warranted, and acknowledge that misapplying herbicide to this wetland-adjacent stand would itself carry ecological risk.
